title: The Sunward Isles
description: An archipelago east across the sea, scattered around Haenara's coasts, home to the Hizurian people. Daimyo hold the islands under a shōgun, and their red-sealed ships carry the eastern trade as far as the Hamlet. Yokai are common in the rivers, the shrines and the shallows, and umibōzu rise in the deep water beyond the reefs. Ships without a Hizurian pilot aboard seldom arrive.
summary: An archipelago of daimyo courts around Haenara, whose haunted waters only its own ships cross safely.

title: Asaumi
description: The great port of the Isles, warehouses and tiled roofs around a deep harbour on the westernmost island. The red-sealed ships sail from here, and every foreign ship that reaches the Isles is met here and given a pilot. Foreign crews trade on the long stone pier and go no further without a daimyo's leave.
summary: The Isles' great port, home of the red-sealed ships, where foreign crews take on Hizurian pilots and wait for leave to go further.

title: The Glass House
description: A noble house on a hill above a harbour town, named for its windows: tall, many-paned and glazed, the only ones of their kind in the Isles. Inside, the rooms are hung with oil portraits and furnished with high-backed chairs and a long dining table. The few staff who remain keep it loosely, with dust on the frames and weeds between the paving stones. Its mistress has not been home in some time.
summary: A noble house of glazed windows and foreign furniture, kept loosely in its mistress's long absence.

title: Kakezuki
description: A coastal rice province of the Sunward Isles, its terraced fields running down to a sheltered shore. A neighbouring clan took it a few years ago in a short war that burned half its villages and broke its ruling house. The fields are worked again under new lords, and the villages are half rebuilt.
summary: A coastal rice province of the Isles, burned and taken in a short war, now worked under new lords.

title: The Issen-ryū Dojo
description: The hall of the Issen-ryū, an ancient iaijutsu school built on a single decisive cut, on a hill above the province's main town. It burned in the war and its master died in it, and its practice floor now lies open to the weather under the fallen roof. The school had one student when it fell, and nobody has taught there since.
summary: The burned hall of an ancient iaijutsu school, roofless and untaught since the war.

title: The Widow's Strait
description: The narrow, fast water between Haenara and the nearest of the isles, its rocks hung with straw ropes and paper talismans. When Haenara took the largest island, the old court fled across it by fleet. Rather than live in disgrace, the empress gave every life aboard to the Tide in exchange for vengeance. The sea took the fleet, and the Isles have been haunted by yokai ever since. Fishermen throw back the crabs in these shallows, whose shells carry scowling faces.
summary: The haunted strait between Haenara and the Isles, its rocks hung with talismans against the drowned.

title: The Drowned Isles
description: The wild interiors and outer coasts of the Sunward Isles, away from the daimyo's roads: mountain passes, old forest, abandoned villages and rocky shore. Yokai and the drowned dead walk here openly, and Hizurians cross it in company and by day.
summary: The haunted wilds of the Sunward Isles, where yokai and the drowned dead walk openly.

title: The Landing
description: A shingle beach under red cliffs, where two dugout boats lie hauled up above the tideline. A torii stands in the shallows a few yards out, and a small shrine on stilts sits against the cliff at the top of a wooden stair.
summary: A shingle beach of hauled-up boats, with a torii standing in the shallows.

title: The Mill Gorge
description: A narrow gorge with a stream running down its floor from a waterfall at the far end. A large wooden waterwheel turns on one side and a thatched hut stands on the other, beside a seated figure carved into a niche in the rock.
summary: A narrow gorge with a waterwheel, a thatched hut and a figure carved into the rock.

title: The Grave Grove
description: A clearing in old forest around a single enormous tree, ringed by rows of stacked stone grave markers and stone lanterns. A rope of twisted straw is tied around a stone at the tree's roots.
summary: A forest cemetery of stone markers and lanterns around one enormous tree.

title: The Valley Village
description: A roadside above a valley of thatched farmhouses, with a notice board on a post and a red maple overhead. One house in the village is burning, and its smoke rises over the hills.
summary: A roadside overlooking a thatched village, where one house is burning.

title: The Bone Road
description: A flagstone road through dark forest, its edges overgrown with broad butterbur leaves. Skeletons hang in the branches on both sides, high above the road.
summary: A flagstone forest road with skeletons caught high in the trees.

title: The Watchtower Fields
description: The edge of a forest, where thick roots break up through the path among clumps of butterbur. A carved marker stone stands at the treeline, and a wooden watchtower rises over the fields beyond.
summary: A forest edge of roots and butterbur, looking out over fields to a watchtower.

title: The Stilt House
description: The covered walkway of a stilt house over still water, with bowls left on its railings and a collapsed stair behind them. Through the fog stands another pier, and more houses on stilts.
summary: The walkway of a stilt house over foggy water, its bowls still on the rails.

title: The Moonlit Bay
description: A shore of dead trees and a stone lantern above a moonlit bay, with a cliff islet across the water. A body hangs from one of the branches, and crows sit in the others.
summary: A moonlit shore of dead trees, crows and one hanged body.

title: The Broken Wood
description: A stretch of forest where every tree has been snapped or uprooted, and the trunks lie fallen across one another. Among the broken trunks stand a woman, a child and a samurai.
summary: A forest of snapped and fallen trees, where three figures stand among the trunks.

title: The Rotting Veranda
description: The covered walkway of a stilt house over still water, its posts and beams crusted thick with fungus. The centre post has snapped, and fog hides the far end of the waterway.
summary: A fungus-crusted stilt-house walkway over foggy water.

title: The Mountain Keep
description: A moonlit pass far below the shōgun's stronghold, a castle keep built into the cliff, with a small torii half-hidden on the slope. A drowned general of the old court walks this road at night. The court above leaves it to him.
summary: The moonlit pass beneath the shōgun's castle, haunted by a drowned general.

title: The Haunted Shore
description: A dark shore of black rock and sea stacks. Over the water, shapes larger than the stacks rise and curl like smoke, and one of them has a face.
summary: A black-rock shore where vast shapes rise from the water.

title: Open Water
description: The deck of a junk under red sails, pitching in heavy seas between pillars of rock. The waves rise without wind, from something moving on the seabed.
summary: The deck of a junk in heavy, windless seas between pillars of rock.
